1	# ADR-0005: Articles revise in place; re-fetch only through the repair queue
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).
6	
7	## Decision
8	
9	Re-acquiring the same URL with materially changed content updates the same article as `revision + 1`; it never creates a new article. Old revision bodies are retained and stay dereferenceable (labeled superseded); search indexes only the latest revision. Automatic re-fetching happens only for quality-flagged acquisitions (suspected truncation or extraction damage) through a repair queue drained by the next Scan, plus a manual refresh command. What forced this: acquisition was one-shot (`fetched_urls` gates a URL forever), so truncated extractions could never heal, and nothing schema-level prevents same-URL duplicate rows once re-fetching exists.
10	
11	## Considered options
12	
13	- Automatic second-look re-fetch of every article after 24-48h: rejected, roughly doubles browser-quota spend on mostly unchanged pages.
14	- Manual refresh only: rejected, in practice truncations would never get repaired.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- Revision comparison uses normalized bodies, so whitespace-level scrape noise cannot mint revisions.
19	- One row per URL becomes schema-enforced.
20	- Live-blog articles are exempt: their mutability is per Live update, not per revision.
